A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Riemannian Consistency Model research. All 23 pages of v1 and 24 pages of v2, including Appendices A–D, are readable and support comparison of the text, equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality experiments on spheres, tori and SO(3), dimensionality experiments, and sampling-efficiency results in Section 4 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments, including the quantitative results in Tables 1–5 and the sampling and visualization studies in Appendix D.

M1.justification: Appendix B.3 corrects the explicit SO(3) differential used in the exact RCM objective: the first term changes from R_u^{-1} J_R(x) v in v1 Eq. 46 to R_u^{-1} v in v2 Eq. 49. This locally revises the specified computation; the general objectives, architecture and sampling algorithms are retained. An implementation change or experimental rerun is not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same Earth-location datasets, checkerboard and protein/RNA torsion datasets, four SO(3) datasets, and high-dimensional Gaussian tori. The added biomedical framing does not introduce another evaluated task or population.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain the same RFM baselines, naive Euclidean consistency comparators, and discrete, continuous and simplified RCM variants. No comparator is added or removed in the main text or appendices.

E3.justification: Appendix C.3 changes the stated tangent-clipping threshold M from 1 to 10. This revises a previously reported training setting, without establishing that experiments were rerun. Dataset sizes, architecture, training budgets, metrics and sampling protocols otherwise remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The dimensionality study in Table 4, NFE sensitivity analysis in Figure 4, timing analysis in Table 5, and qualitative comparisons in Appendix D are retained. No new ablation, robustness test or supplementary analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests for the performance results. v2 introduces no uncertainty-reporting or statistical-estimation changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 retain their numerical results, and Figures 3–6 retain the same curves and generated-sample visualizations. The revised SO(3) formulas and clipping setting are not accompanied by new or replacement empirical results.

T1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a first-order exponential-map expansion, repairs perturbation formulas by subtracting the unperturbed value and replacing J_L(u) with J_L(x), and derives the Jacobian cancellation underlying the corrected base-point differential. These are substantive but localized mathematical corrections; the main theorems and proposition remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims of manifold-respecting consistency modeling, RCD/RCT equivalence, simplified training and improved few-step generation are retained. The abstract's added RNA/protein wording highlights applications already represented in v1 rather than introducing a new core contribution.

C2.justification: The introduction newly links 200–1000 sampling steps in protein-design models to limited virtual-screening throughput and argues that few-step generation could accelerate drug discovery and enzyme design. This adds an application-impact argument; benchmark interpretations and the sampling-quality qualifications in Appendix D remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds an explicit code-availability statement and repository address in the abstract, revises the documented clipping threshold, and provides a more explicit SO(3) differential calculation. The remaining architecture, optimizer, hardware and training-time disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: The same 59 references and related-work discussion are retained. The positioning of RCM relative to Riemannian generative models and Euclidean consistency models, including its novelty claim, is unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized additions to the abstract and introduction, expands the SO(3) derivation, and adds a funding acknowledgement. The overall section structure and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All six figures and five tables are retained without redesign. Equation spacing, reference spacing and placement relative to surrounding text change; for example, Table 3 now precedes its interpretation and Figure 4 precedes the final NFE discussion bullet. These are limited layout revisions.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects erroneous SO(3) perturbation formulas and supplies the missing Jacobian-cancellation derivation in Appendix B.3, improving mathematical consistency and implementation guidance. The code-access pointer also improves usability. These gains are limited: empirical evidence is unchanged, the clipping-threshold revision is not explained as a correction or rerun, and the broader biomedical-impact argument receives no additional downstream validation.
